activities.title: Evaluate an OKR
reference: Objectives are inspirational, clear, and memorable, and classified as a roofshot or a moonshot.
Key Results are value-based, measurable, and gradable.

referenceDefinitions.roofshot: A Roofshot is a conservative pursuit: lower-risk, with highly likely and tangible results. Optimization work fits naturally here.
referenceDefinitions.moonshot: A Moonshot is a very ambitious pursuit that aims for an innovative step change. The risk is expected to be high, but the goal is not impossible. The point of a moonshot is to push past small, safe optimizations and revisit how the problem is solved today, in the hope of a breakthrough.

rows: Objective: "Modernize our platform."
KR1: Migrate 80% of services to the new architecture.
KR2: Reduce deployment time by 30%.
KR3: Complete the migration ahead of the Q3 roadmap deadline.

fields.label: What's wrong, or what's missing?
Would this OKR make it obvious what to prioritize?

lessons.title: Creating an AI-Native ART launch plan
objectives: Resolve gaps from your assessment into specific, owned actions
Build a launch plan that sequences these actions before PI Outcome Planning, before Sense and Respond, or after both
Commit to the plan as a group
Discuss how you will share your plan and prepare for what happens after this class

activities.title: The AI-Native implementation launch plan
activities.intro: Access the Assessment Tool to build, commit, and enact your plan to launch your AI-Native ART.

fields.label: Final reflections and notes

activities.title: Resolve each identified gap
activities.intro: For each gap, there are three options: Accept it for now and take no further action. Place the gap onto the launch plan at the point when you plan to address it. Or create a specific action for addressing it — multiple gaps can be added to a single action. For each Gap and Action, add an Owner.
columns: Decision (Accept / Place on plan / Create action)
When (Before PI Outcome Planning / Before Sense and Respond / After both)

activities.title: Review the AI-Native ART launch plan
activities.intro: As each gap was resolved, a draft AI-Native Launch Plan was created. Review the plan individually looking for missing items, risks, or opportunities. Discuss these in your group. Share as a class.

fields.label: What is missing?
What risk is not accounted for?
What opportunity has the plan not taken?
Is the load balanced across the three groups, or is almost everything sitting before the first event?

activities.title: Determine the dates for the AI-Native ART events
activities.intro: As a class, agree on two real dates. Add both to your launch plan. Everything in your plan now has a real deadline to build toward.

fields.label: Your first PI Outcome Planning event
Your first Sense and Respond event
If you can't set a date today, who decides it and by when?

activities.title: Adjust the AI-Native ART launch plan
activities.intro: Based on the previous review, agree on the necessary adjustments to resolve any outstanding items, and update the plan to reflect them.

activities.title: Commit to the AI-Native ART launch plan
activities.intro: Before this plan is final, determine if the group actually agrees with it. Take a minute on your own and look back at the plan. On the count of three, everyone holds up a fist of five — a closed fist means no confidence, five fingers means full confidence.

fields.label: If you're at three or below, what would have to change?
fields.helper: Anyone showing three or below explains why before the plan moves forward.

fields.label: What concerns were raised, and how were they addressed?

activities.title: Share your plan
activities.intro: As a class, consider who needs to see this plan and how you will share it with them. Name the people, the format, and what you need from them when they see it.
reference: Prompts to cover: Communicating · Team Training and launching the teams · AI training · Iterating the plan as you learn more · Owners reporting back · Measuring progress
columns: Who needs to see it (a real name)
What you need from them (approval / feedback / awareness)

fields.label: What is your ongoing plan for communication?
fields.helper: The AI-Native Launch Plan is a living document.

activities.title: Reflect on what you've learned
activities.intro: Think back across the whole two days. As a class, discuss:

fields.label: What's one thing you'll do differently when you're back at work because of this course?
What surprised you — about your ART, or about AI-Native SAFe itself?

activities.title: What's next
activities.intro: Your launch plan is not the end. It's the starting point for the next phase of the roadmap: implement the critical success factors, in the order you just built.
reference: The plan moves only if the named owners act. Nobody else is going to pick this up after the class ends.
